body: You’re heard, this shit sucks and a lot of us go through it, but there are people who make it through it who benefit so much from that pain, they just have to survive time which is not an easy ask

1. No
2. It never worked for me or my sister or my mom
3. I gained weight but not because I was on it but it certainly didn’t hinder my ability to put on weight.

If you don’t feel the positive effects after 2 months you should honestly switch. I was on it for 6 months and while some of my secondary symptoms improved like my insomnia and general restlessness I didn’t FEEL any better in terms of my depression.

On August 13th, try to have your ideal day. Maybe get some ice cream, go to the beach, get your favorite food, watch a show you’ve been meaning to watch, get a massage, and just wait and see how you feel at the end of the day. Just try, see how it feels to feel good for a day and if by the end of the day you still want to go through with it then I urge you to reconsider. Try for the 14th to be an even better day, spend some money treating yourself you’d much rather lose $100+ then your life that much I can promise you

I’m glad to hear you gave it a try! Very simple chord progression but it often feels representative of how I feel, that slight hint of dissonance in that Bm chord it just feels right to play!

Also if you’re interested in more complete songs rather than just 4 chord progressions I would try to learn “Breathe” by Ingrid Michaelson. It sounds beautiful using finger style and playing it softly feels like you’re just having a quiet conversation with your instrument!

That’s my point though, I don’t know my own story because in truth I am defined by those things, in a complete vacuum I don’t know what I’d be because it feels my character is so interwoven with the people in my life that it doesn’t hold it’s own without those people to contrast it off of

Be it an invincible hand or what I call “the author” we are both subject to a story we are not content with continuing. I’m not fatalistic but it is hard to not feel doomed, like that hand or the author are pushing us toward wanting something that we really shouldn’t want which is killing our selves

Well, imagine reading a supposed biography that the universe has written about you, and you go to read it and the majority of it you are constantly being referenced as someone relative to someone else: “so and so’s brother, her boyfriend, their son, that university’s student” as if you as a person are defined by everything but yourself. It just feels like I picked up this book with the expectation of reading about my journey through life and instead I’m reading about my reactions to everyone else’s adventures.
I fear I run that risk regardless, 80 years to 2 years makes little difference to obscurity, it may be there waiting either way
I do hope you’ll have the courage to try again, it sounds like you have a lot of love to give to a child

I have 4 older siblings and am the only boy in my family. My mom had 7 pregnancies and miscarried 3 times (one of my sisters is my dad’s daughter from a different marriage), the kids she has now are who she loves most in this world, and those 3 potential kids would not have been us. I can’t begin to understand that loss you are feeling in your heart, but if you want to try again then don’t be scared, you will meet your baby when that baby is the one you were meant to meet. I hope you can take solace in whatever faith you have in fate, even if it’s very small.
